clue.text: City district with no hotel

indicators.note: 'with no' tells us a letter is dropped from the district word

parts.note: a parish is a small local district
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood of a town that has no hotel in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City' looks like it qualifies 'district', but it is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: The French capital is a well-known example of a city.

clue.text: African explorer follows latitude line to manoeuvre into bay

indicators.note: the explorer's name comes after the line of latitude, so it sits second

parts.note: a parallel is a line of latitude on a map
Mungo Park was a Scottish explorer of the Niger in West Africa

explanation.surface: An explorer in Africa tracks a line of latitude and then steers his boat into a bay.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's bay is a coastal inlet; the definition's bay is a parking space beside the kerb.
explanation.definitionFit: To reverse a car into a roadside space alongside the kerb is to slot it into a bay.

clue.text: What's regularly taken round in party in Agra?

definitions.text: What's regularly taken round in party in Agra?

indicators.note: 'taken round' turns the chosen letters back to front
'regularly' picks every other letter of the phrase party in Agra

explanation.surface: A question about what gets handed round at a gathering in the Indian city of Agra.
explanation.walkthrough: Every second letter of PARTY IN AGRA gives ATIAR, which 'taken round' reverses. The whole clue also works as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This yoghurt side dish is served with Indian meals, so it could well be passed around at a party in Agra.

clue.text: The woman will dismiss flak, perhaps

parts.note: 'she'll' is the short form of 'she will'
to fire someone is to dismiss them from a job

explanation.surface: A woman intends to sack someone, which may draw criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: Flak means criticism on the surface but is anti-aircraft fire here; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Flak is bursting anti-aircraft shells, one kind of artillery bombardment.

clue.text: Wartime worker with doctor going back into lines

indicators.note: 'going into' puts the pieces between the two letters for lines

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line, so LL is lines
'and' can mean along with

indicators.note: 'going back' turns the word for doctor around

parts.note: to rig something is to doctor or tamper with it

explanation.surface: A wartime employee and a doctor retreat into the lines of defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like a person, but it is a verb meaning to tamper; 'going back' reverses it to GIR. The Land Army was Britain's wartime female farm workforce.
explanation.definitionFit: Women in Britain's Women's Land Army farmed the land during both world wars.

clue.text: Section of latrine needing trough emptied

indicators.note: 'emptied' removes the insides of each of the three words, leaving only the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Part of a toilet block whose trough needs clearing out.
explanation.definitionFit: A length of pipe or cloth is a piece or section of it.

clue.text: Talent for finding underground bar for a quick drop

parts.note: a nose is a knack for sniffing things out, as in 'a nose for news'
a dive is a seedy bar, often in a basement

explanation.surface: A knack for locating a basement pub where you can pop in for a quick drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drop' suggests a drop of drink in the bar, but here it is a sudden fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A steep plunge, as of an aircraft or share prices, is a rapid fall.

clue.text: Robot to operate lunar excursion module

parts.note: a machine that goes is working or operating
LEM is the abbreviation for the Apollo lunar excursion module

explanation.surface: A robot built to drive the moon lander.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jewish folklore this is a clay figure brought to life, so an artificial servant like an automaton.

clue.text: Note wave-riding champ come up again

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
to surf is to ride the waves
an ace is a champion or expert

explanation.surface: A message about a champion surfer bobbing back up out of the waves.
explanation.definitionFit: A submarine or a diver rising to the top of the water once more does exactly this.

clue.text: Bring up a small and good girl to drink wine for health?

parts.note: to raise children is to bring them up
'a' can mean one
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: Bring up a modest, well-behaved daughter to drink wine for her health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bring up' reads as rearing a child; it is the word for lifting. 'for health?' asks us to read it as a toast to someone's health.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifting a glass of wine while wishing someone good health is the act of toasting them.

clue.text: An author's weakness — what might be said about Quentin Crisp hugging queen?

indicators.note: 'hugging' means the description wraps around the letter for queen

parts.words: what might be said about Quentin Crisp
parts.note: Quentin Crisp was a famously flamboyant author, so one might say 'writer's camp'
R is short for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A writer's flaw, illustrated by a comment about the flamboyant author Quentin Crisp embracing a queen.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside CAMP to make CRAMP. Quentin Crisp was an English writer and raconteur known for his camp manner.
explanation.definitionFit: A painful spasm in the hand from long periods with a pen is a writer's physical affliction.

clue.text: Guide round Lima during festival handed out bills

indicators.note: 'round' puts the word for guide around everything else

parts.note: to lead is to guide

indicators.note: 'during' puts the Lima letter inside the festival word

parts.note: a fete is a festival or fair
L is Lima in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone showing visitors around Lima's festival was handing out bills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lima' is not the Peruvian capital but the radio code word for L; 'during' gives FLETE, which 'round' encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: To leaflet is to hand out flyers, which are printed bills or notices.

clue.text: Nearly get wed without ring and symbolic meal

indicators.note: 'without' in the sense of outside: the shortened word goes around the ring
'Nearly' drops the last letter of the word for getting wed

parts.note: to marry is to get wed
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A couple almost married without a ring, then shared a meaningful dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: MARR goes around O. 'without' here means outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: The bitter herbs eaten at the Passover Seder stand for slavery, a symbolic part of that ritual dinner.

clue.text: Name this setter over something that comes up again

indicators.note: 'over' turns the phrase back to front

parts.note: to cite someone is to name them
the setter refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: The setter asks to be named for a theme that keeps recurring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes up again' sounds like a recurring topic; it means being sick.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug that induces vomiting makes the stomach's contents rise a second time.

clue.text: Unprepared before accepting Times rate

indicators.note: 'accepting' means the word for before takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
X is the multiplication sign, read as times
tempo is a rate or speed

explanation.surface: Unready, until the newspaper accepted the fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is the multiplication sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A speech given off the cuff, without rehearsal, is impromptu.

clue.text: Beware over aunt brewing purgative medicine

indicators.note: 'over' turns the Latin warning word around

parts.note: cave is Latin for beware, used as a schoolboy warning

indicators.note: 'brewing' says the letters of aunt are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A warning that an aunt is concocting a laxative remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: CAVE reversed gives EVAC; 'brewing' rearranges AUNT into UANT.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a drug that empties the bowels, a laxative or purgative.

clue.text: Bashful around papa over proper form of protection

indicators.note: in a down entry 'over' places the first part above the next
'around' wraps the word for bashful about the papa letter

parts.note: coy means bashful
P is Papa in the NATO phonetic alphabet
right means proper or correct

explanation.surface: A shy person shielding their father, with a proper kind of safeguard.
explanation.definitionFit: This legal right protects authors and artists from unauthorised copying of their work.

clue.text: Individual copies turned up to evaluate

indicators.note: in a down entry 'turned up' reads the word upward, so backwards

parts.note: apes copies
to rate is to evaluate

explanation.surface: A single set of copies turns up to be assessed.
explanation.definitionFit: Distinct and apart from the others, as in 'two separate rooms', means individual.

clue.text: Almost killed before warning light is moved with no urgency

indicators.note: the shortened word comes first, ahead of the light
'Almost' drops the last letter of the word for killed

parts.note: to pot game is to shoot it
a red light is a warning

explanation.surface: Nearly killed before a warning light moved slowly into place.
explanation.definitionFit: To potter about is to move around in an unhurried, aimless way.

clue.text: Computer program needs attention to be published

parts.note: an app is a computer program
to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: Software needing someone's notice before it can be released.
explanation.definitionFit: A book or article that comes out in print is said to come out or be issued.

clue.text: Scholar's leading part in standard assessment task

indicators.note: 'in' puts the leading part inside the test's initials

parts.note: SAT is a standard assessment task, a national test sat by schoolchildren in England
the van is the leading part of an army or movement

explanation.surface: A student's top section in a national school test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading part' looks like a first letter, but it is VAN as in vanguard.
explanation.definitionFit: A learned person of great knowledge is a scholar.

clue.text: Lover's letter read out

definitions.meaning: Shakespeare's young man in love with Juliet stands for any lover
the spoken word used for R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A love letter recited.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's hero is the archetypal lover, and his name is the radio code word for R.

clue.text: Lubricated like a spring, but not with carbon

indicators.note: 'not with' signals the carbon letter is removed

parts.note: a spring is wound up, coiled
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: A spring that was greased but without carbon.
explanation.definitionFit: Greasing machinery with a slippery fluid lubricates it.

clue.text: Going without oxygen, coming round in panic I bore an airhole

indicators.note: 'coming round' says the letters are read backwards
'in' says the answer lies inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Without air and starting to panic, I drill a breathing hole.
explanation.walkthrough: The run 'c I bore an a' inside 'panic I bore an airhole' reads backwards to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Organisms or exercise that work without air or oxygen are described this way.

clue.text: Uproar of billions over murdered brother

indicators.note: in a down entry 'over' places the billions letter above the brother

parts.note: Abel was killed by his brother Cain in Genesis

explanation.surface: An uproar involving billions over a brother's murder.
explanation.definitionFit: From the Tower of Babel, the word means a noisy confusion of voices.

clue.text: Logical system error mostly with unfruitful broken lab gear

indicators.note: 'mostly' drops the last letter of the word for error

parts.note: a boob is a blunder or error
lean means meagre or unproductive, as in lean years

indicators.note: 'broken' says the letters of lab gear are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A broken piece of lab kit, a barren result and an error mostly undermine a system.
explanation.walkthrough: BOOB loses its last letter to give BOO; 'broken' rearranges LAB GEAR into ALGEBRA.
explanation.definitionFit: George Boole's algebra of true and false values underpins digital logic.

clue.text: Support for driver re deaths in a crash

indicators.note: 'in a crash' says the letters of re deaths are smashed up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A safety device for motorists, regarding deaths in a car crash.
explanation.definitionFit: The cushion on top of a car seat supports the driver's head, protecting against whiplash.

clue.text: Plant that flowers, ending around the middle of July

indicators.note: 'around' puts the word for ending around the centre of July

parts.note: a tip is an end or point

indicators.note: 'the middle of' takes the central letters of July

explanation.surface: A flowering plant whose blooms finish around mid-July.
explanation.definitionFit: This spring-flowering bulb is a familiar garden plant.
